sections.title: -nál/-nél for who you work for
sections.content: You already use -nál/-nél for "at someone's place," like a fogorvosnál ("at the dentist's"). Hungarian reuses the very same suffix for naming your employer: dolgozik with a company or person in -nál/-nél means "to work for." Kinél dolgozol? asks "Who do you work for?" — literally "at whose place do you work?"

items.spanish: Üzletember vagyok, és egy nagy cégnél dolgozom.
items.english: I'm a businessperson, and I work for a big company.

items.spanish: Károly mérnök, és egy cégnél dolgozik.
items.english: Károly is an engineer, and he works for a company.

sections.content: Hol dolgozol? asks about the physical place (egy irodában), while Kinél dolgozol? asks about the employer (egy cégnél) — the two questions can have completely different answers, since your office and your employer aren't always the same thing.
